question: Where did HTTP 200 Content-Type text/plain body OK come from?
method: route attribution by differential probing, then direct-to-host comparison

directToHostControlProbe.observed: HTTP 401 application/json from cloudflare (a real upstream answer)

conclusion: The OK is NOT application code, not a route stub, not a dev fallback and not an upstream pass-through of a real provider answer. models.github.ai is intercepted at the network egress boundary of this environment and answers 200 text/plain 'OK' for every path, with or without a credential, while the same egress reaches Groq normally. The broker, being a faithful proxy, forwarded that as a successful completion.
boundary: Outside the application's control: the host cannot be reached from here. There is no application fix that makes models.github.ai answer.
appDefectExposed: The broker treated any 2xx as a completion. That IS inside the application and is repaired in Gate B.
credentialSourceClassification: server-side broker credential (env) — value never logged
